title: Finite stalk identity lifts to a linear section map
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring. Let $G$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. For an algebraically closed geometric point $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, suppose its geometric stalk $M=G_s$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is finite as a set. There is a pointed etale neighbourhood $(U,a)$ of $s$ and a $\Lambda$-linear map $f:M\to G(U)$ such that $\operatorname{germ}_a\circ f=\operatorname{id}_M$. No Noetherian hypothesis is needed.

proof.text: Represent all elements of M by section germs. Cofilteredness puts their finitely many pointed neighbourhoods under a common pointed neighbourhood; restriction gives representatives there.

source.place: Tag 0GKC, lemma-characterize-locally-constant-module, finite-presentation paragraph, expanded using the finite operation table

proof.text: Index the addition relations by M × M and the scalar relations by Λ × M. Their two sides have equal germs. Inductively apply eventual equality and restrict the earlier relations to obtain one pointed refinement where every relation holds.

source.place: Tag 0GKC, lemma-characterize-locally-constant-module, finite-presentation paragraph, expanded using the finite operation table

proof.text: The representatives now define a linear map, and the prescribed germs show that its composite with the germ map is the identity. Additivity implies the zero relation, including for the zero ring.

theorem exists_etale_finite_stalk_section
    {S : Scheme.{u}} {Λ : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    (G : Sheaf S.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S)
    [Finite (↑((pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiber.obj G) : Type (u + 1))] :
    ∃ (U : S.Etale) (a : (pointSmallEtale s).fiber.obj U)
      (f : (pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiber.obj G ⟶ G.obj.obj (op U)),
      f ≫ (pointSmallEtale s).toPresheafFiber U a G.obj = 𝟙 _
